previous_disclosures.summary: The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical with severe downturns driven by supply/demand imbalances, price erosion, and economic weakness; AMD has incurred substantial losses in past downturns due to declines in average selling prices and excess inventory, and its financial performance may continue to be negatively affected by these fluctuations and global economic uncertainty.

AMD's growth depends on demand from high-growth emerging global markets, requiring adequate local infrastructure and relationships; if demand from these markets is below expectations, sales may decrease materially.
Demand for AMD's products depends on market conditions in sold industries, and fluctuations in demand or market declines in these industries could materially adversely affect results of operations.
Industry-wide fluctuations in the computer marketplace have materially adversely affected AMD in the past and may continue to do so in the future.

AMD experiences significant demand for AI accelerators optimized for generative AI applications since Q4 2023, but this demand depends on customer utilization of generative AI solutions, the near-term and long-term trajectory of which is unknown; failure to develop products, keep pace with competitors, or adapt to changes could adversely affect the business.

Client segment revenue depends on AI PC adoption; while AMD is building AI capabilities like Ryzen AI into Client products, adoption pace is uncertain; past revenue declines in Client and Gaming segments have been driven by form factor changes, competition, and replacement cycle changes.

GPU revenue has historically been affected by cryptocurrency mining market volatility, and inability to manage risks related to this volatility, including potential actions by global monetary authorities, could materially adversely affect the GPU business.

The success of semi-custom SoC products in the Gaming segment depends on securing customers for the design pipeline and consumer market conditions, including the success of game console systems for Sony and Microsoft.

The Embedded segment, including CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, and Adaptive SoC products, is subject to macroeconomic trends and volatile business conditions; customers may draw down inventory and order less, as evidenced by Embedded segment revenue decreasing in 2024 as customers normalized inventory levels.

current_disclosures.summary: AMD’s business is vulnerable to the highly cyclical nature of the semiconductor industry, which causes substantial declines in average selling prices and inventory adjustments. Growth depends on demand from high-growth emerging markets and varies across Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded segments. Specific risks include unknown AI infrastructure adoption trajectories, energy and capital constraints for data center buildouts, uncertain AI PC adoption rates, crypto market volatility affecting Gaming GPUs, and embedded customer inventory drawdowns due to macroeconomic trends.

comparisons.peer_topic: System-Level Solution Development and Margin Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Development of system-level memory and storage products involves higher per-unit manufacturing costs, longer development cycles, and significant dependence on customer specifications and purchasing volumes, which may result in reduced profits if costs are not offset by higher prices.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron disclose that their business success for specific product categories depends on meeting customer specifications and securing customer purchasing volumes. AMD’s Gaming segment success relies on securing customers for its semi-custom SoC design pipeline and the consumer market success of console systems. Similarly, Micron states that its system-level memory and storage solutions depend on meeting customer specifications and customers choosing Micron's products over competitors at sufficient volumes and prices. Both highlight the dependency on the end-customer's ability to create, market, and sell products successfully.

sentences.text: The success of our semi-custom SoC products in our Gaming segment is dependent on securing customers for our semi-custom design pipeline and consumer market conditions, including the success of game console systems and next generation consoles for Sony and Microsoft.
Our development of system-level memory and storage products is dependent, in part, upon successfully identifying and meeting our customers' specifications for those products.

Even if our products meet customer specifications, our sales of system-level solutions are dependent upon our customers choosing our products over those of our competitors and purchasing our products at sufficient volumes and prices.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks of R&D investments in markets with limited history
comparisons.peer_summary: Investments in research and development for markets where NVIDIA has a limited operating history may not produce meaningful revenue for several years or at all, particularly if new products fail to obtain design wins or achieve widespread adoption.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA face risks related to the success of new product designs and the process of securing customer adoption (design wins). AMD’s Gaming segment success depends on securing customers for its semi-custom design pipeline. NVIDIA discloses that obtaining design wins is a lengthy process dependent on anticipating customer demands and that failure to obtain design wins or ensure product value can prevent future revenue. Both companies highlight the uncertainty in converting technical development into commercial success with key customers.

sentences.text: The success of our semi-custom SoC products in our Gaming segment is dependent on securing customers for our semi-custom design pipeline and consumer market conditions, including the success of game console systems and next generation consoles for Sony and Microsoft.
If we fail to develop or monetize new products and technologies, or if they do not become widely adopted, our financial results could be adversely affected.
Obtaining design wins may involve a lengthy process and depends on our ability to anticipate and provide features and functionality that customers will demand.

comparisons.peer_topic: Revenue Fluctuations from Customer Product Cycles
comparisons.peer_summary: Timing and size of purchases may be impacted by customer product introductions, over which Qualcomm has no control, causing revenues and results of operations to fluctuate.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm disclose that their revenue and business success are dependent on customer product introductions and market success over which the company has no control. AMD states its Gaming segment success depends on consumer market conditions, including the success of game console systems for Sony and Microsoft. Qualcomm states that the timing and size of purchases by significant customers may be impacted by the timing and success of their new product introductions. Both identify the dependency on the end-market performance of their customers' devices as a key risk.

sentences.text: The success of our semi-custom SoC products in our Gaming segment is dependent on securing customers for our semi-custom design pipeline and consumer market conditions, including the success of game console systems and next generation consoles for Sony and Microsoft.

In addition, the timing and size of purchases by our significant customers may be impacted by the timing of such customers' new or next generation product introductions, over which we have no control, and the timing and success of such introductions may cause our revenues and results of operations to fluctuate.
